CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems

Classical Baselines You Have To Beat

Session 11  ·  M3 - Detection, from Baselines to Models
Outcomes: CO2, CO3  ·  Dr. Gonzalo D Parra
1

Learning Objectives

By the end of this session you will be able to:

  1. - State the score a model has to beat before it has done anything at all, and quote it beside every score you publish.
  2. - Explain what each of five classical models is actually doing, in one sentence each, using the matrix you built last session.
  3. - Follow one test row through a model by hand, and follow a second row that the same model gets wrong.
  4. - Read a training score, a cross-validation score and a test score as three different claims, and say what each one cannot see.
  5. - Choose a model with a written reason that is not its accuracy.

Before a Model, a Floor

  • Every score means nothing until you know what doing nothing scores. That number is where this session starts.

The Model That Never Looks

  • An everyday version. A smoke alarm that is disconnected is right on every day there is no fire. Its score is high and its value is zero.
DefinitionThe floor. The score of the best model that ignores the data: answer the most common class, every time, whatever the row says.

on the training file0.5350 of 58,630
on the test file0.4310 of 12,833

The Floor, Drawn

6

Decide: the Rule for Every Score in This Course

  1. 1Rule: never write an accuracy without the floor for that same file beside it.
  2. 2On the test file, 0.431 is free. A model at 0.60 has bought you 17 points for all your work.
  3. 3A model below 0.431 on test is worse than a disconnected alarm, and you would not know from the number alone.
TipWrite the floor at the top of your report before you fit anything. Teams that do this stop being impressed by 80 percent.

Model One, Ask the Neighbours

  • The question: this row is new. Which rows that I have already seen does it look like?
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
8

The Rule Everybody Already Uses

  • An everyday version. You move to a new street and want to know which school is good. You ask the five nearest houses and go with the majority.
Definitionk-nearest neighbours. Keep every training row. To classify a new row, measure the distance to all of them, take the K closest, and answer with the majority label among those K.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
9

Find It in the Matrix: What "Near" Means

  1. 1Distance is measured across the 107 columns of the matrix you saved last session, one number per column.
  2. 2It only means anything because you standardized: before scaling, src_bytes ran to 1.4 billion and count stopped at 511, so distance would have been a measure of bytes and nothing else.
  3. 3For the next three slides we use two of those columns, so the distances fit on a screen: src_bytes after the log, and dst_host_srv_count.
Watch outk-NN is the model that punishes an unscaled column hardest, because the column with the biggest numbers becomes the only column that counts.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems

Why the Second One Failed, and It Is Not the Model

Share of the training fileShare of the test file
R2L rows0.79 percent12.80 percent
  1. 1Both examples are R2L. In the file the model learned from, R2L is fewer than eight rows in a thousand.
  2. 2So the neighbourhood around an R2L row is full of normal rows, and the majority is normal. The rule worked exactly as written.
  3. 3This is the imbalance you measured last session, arriving as a wrong answer on a real row.
Why it mattersA model does not fail because it is a bad idea. It fails where its training file was thin, and you can predict where that is before you fit anything.

15

What K Does to the Whole Space

  • The same two columns, with the answer the rule would give at every point on the screen.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
16

Read the Two Boundaries

  1. 1K=1 trusts one row. Every stray attack in a normal neighbourhood becomes its own red island, and any test row that lands there is called an attack.
  2. 2K=51 asks fifty-one rows, so a single stray cannot make an island. The border is smooth and the small islands are gone.
  3. 3On these two columns alone, K=1 scores 0.783 on the test file and K=51 scores 0.793. On all 107 columns, K=5 scores 0.780.
DefinitionOverfitting, seen for the first time. K=1 fits the training rows perfectly, because the nearest row to a training row is itself. It is the smallest K and the worst idea.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
17

Decide: K, and Where This Model Cannot Go

FitAnswer all 22,544 test rowsAnswer one row
k-nearest neighbours, K=50.01 s1.08 s0.0023 s
decision tree, unlimited0.51 s0.00 s0.0001 s
  1. 1Decide K by cross-validation, never by which K scores best on the test file. Odd numbers only, so a two-class vote cannot tie.
  2. 2Decide against k-NN for a sensor. It does no work when you fit it and all of the work on every question, forever. A tree answers one row twenty times faster.
Why it mattersA detector answers at prediction time, on every connection, all year. The model that is slow to fit and fast to answer is almost always the right trade here.

Model Two, One Weight per Column

  • The question: instead of storing every row, can a model store one number per column and still answer?
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
19

The Scorecard

  • An everyday version. A shop gives you points: two for a coffee, five for a sandwich, minus three for a returned item. Add your points and cross a line to get the free drink.
DefinitionLogistic regression. One weight per column. Multiply each column by its weight, add them all up, then squeeze the total into a probability between 0 and 1 with an S-shaped curve.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
20

One Column In, an S-Curve Out

  • Fitted on count alone, so the whole model fits on one screen. The red dots are the real attack share of the rows in each slice of the axis.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
21

Read the Curve

  1. 1The weight on count is 2.03 and the intercept is 0.158, so a row one standard deviation above average lands at about 0.90 probability.
  2. 2The red dots are what the file actually does: in each slice of the axis, the share of rows that really are attacks. The curve follows them, which is what "the model fits" means here.
  3. 3On that one column alone it scores 0.651 on the test file. That is above the 0.431 floor and far below the 0.761 the full 107 columns reach.
NoteA model you can draw on one axis is worth fitting once, even when you will not use it. It is the cheapest way to see what one column knows.

23

Read the Weights

  1. 1flag=S0 is a connection that was opened and never answered, which is what a port scan leaves behind. The model found that without being told.
  2. 2root_shell is a flag that says a session got root. It is one of 107 columns and it is the fourth strongest push toward attack.
  3. 3The weights are comparable only because every column was standardized last session. On raw columns the biggest weight would mark the smallest unit.
Watch outA weight is a pattern in this file, not a cause. service=IRC leaning normal is a fact about this traffic, not advice about IRC.

Decide: Where to Put the Line

  1. 1The model hands you a probability. You choose the number above which it is called an attack; 0.5 is only the default.
  2. 2Move the line down and you catch more attacks and raise more false alarms. Move it up and the opposite.
  3. 3Decision for now: keep 0.5 and report per class. Lecture 12 turns that line into a budget you can defend.

Model Three, One Question at a Time

  • The question: can a model be a list of yes and no questions that a person could read out loud?
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
26

Twenty Questions, Played on a File

  • An everyday version. Guess the animal in twenty questions. Every good question splits what is left into two groups that are more alike than the group you started with.
DefinitionDecision tree. Find the one question that best splits the rows into an attack-heavy group and a normal-heavy group. Then ask the same thing again inside each group, until a stopping rule says enough.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems

WhereRows that arriveError if we stop here
the root, before any question67,343 normal, 58,630 attack0.465

  • Error here means: if the box had to answer with its own majority, how often would it be wrong.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
29

The Arithmetic of One Split

  1. 1Before the first question, the best you can do is answer normal for everything and be wrong 46.5 percent of the time.
  2. 2After two questions, each box answers with its own majority, and the four boxes together are wrong 7.8 percent of the time.
  3. 30.465 to 0.078, from two questions written in words a person can read. That box with 52,211 attacks and 1,707 normal rows is small-byte non-http traffic, which is a denial-of-service flood.
Why it mattersThis is why trees are the model you show an analyst. The path to an answer is a sentence, and a sentence can be argued with.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
30

How a Tree Scores a Question

  • To pick the best question, the tree needs a number for how mixed a group is. There are three in common use.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
31

Three Ways to Score a Mixed Group

  • Each curve is a score against the share of attack rows in the box. All three are 0 when the box is pure and worst when it is half and half.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
32

Read the Three Curves, and Why It Matters

  1. 1Classification error is two straight lines. Straight lines are the problem: a split can move rows around without moving the total at all, so the tree sees no gain and stops early.
  2. 2Gini and entropy are curved. Any split that makes one side purer lowers the total, even when the majority in both boxes stays the same, so the tree keeps finding useful questions.
  3. 3Our trees use Gini, which is what scikit-learn does unless you say otherwise.
TipYou do not need the formulas. You need to know that the tool's default scoring is curved on purpose, and that a straight-line score would have stopped your tree two questions in.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
33

How Deep Should It Go?

  • The same tree fitted again and again, allowed one more question each time, scored three different ways.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
34

Read the Depth Curve, Including the Awkward Part

  1. 1The grey and green lines never differ by more than 0.002. Cross-validation held rows back, and still agreed with the training score almost exactly.
  2. 2Cross-validation is highest at the deepest tree tested, depth 30. If you chose depth by cross-validation alone, you would take the deepest tree available.
  3. 3The test file disagrees: its best depth is 4, and every depth from 1 to 30 lands between 0.776 and 0.816. Depth barely matters there.
Watch outCross-validation only ever holds back rows from the training file. It cannot hold back an attack type that the training file never contained, and the test file is full of those. That gap is the whole story of this session.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
35

Decide: Take the Tree You Can Read

TreeLeavesTrainTest
depth 5230.9880.794
unlimited (depth 28)2691.0000.797
  1. 1246 extra leaves buy 0.003 on the test file, which is inside the noise you will measure two slides from now.
  2. 2Decision: depth 5. Twenty-three leaves is a page you can hand to an analyst; 269 is not.
  3. 3The unlimited tree scoring 1.000 on training is textbook overfitting, and it still generalised as well as any of them. A perfect training score is a warning to investigate, not a verdict.

Model Four, Multiply the Odds

  • The question: Lecture 4 counted how often each value appears in attack rows and in normal rows. Can those count tables be the whole model?

The Rule of Thumb

  • An everyday version. A doctor sees a cough, a fever and a rash. Each one on its own makes one illness a bit more likely; together they make it much more likely.
DefinitionNaive Bayes. For each value of each column, count how often it appears in attack rows and in normal rows. To classify a new row, start from the overall share of attacks and multiply by the ratio each of its values carries.

Every Value of One Column, as a Push

  • How far each flag value moves the odds, with the rows behind it. One step up the axis multiplies the odds of attack by ten.

42

Read the Pushes, and Name the Naive Part

  1. 1S0 appears in 34,497 attack rows and 354 normal rows. On its own it is nearly a verdict, and the model gets that from counting, not from training.
  2. 2SF, a connection that completed normally, is the opposite: 63,393 normal rows against 11,552 attack rows.
  3. 3The model multiplies these pushes together as if the columns were independent. That is the "naive" part, and Lecture 4 measured that they are not: service and flag move together.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
43

Decide: Keep It, and Say Why

  1. 1It scores 0.766 on the test file, beating logistic regression at 0.761, from the nominal columns alone and a fit of 0.05 seconds.
  2. 2Its attack recall on the test file is 0.669, the best of the five models in this session.
  3. 3Decision: keep it as the fast, explainable baseline. Its assumption is false on this data, and it still beats a model that had all 107 columns. Say both of those things when you report it.
Why it mattersA model whose assumption is known to be wrong and whose score is good is not a paradox. It is a reminder that the assumption is a convenience, not a claim about the world.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
44

Model Five, Ask Many Trees

  • The question: one tree memorised its training file. What happens if we grow many of them and let them vote?
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
45

The Panel

  • An everyday version. One doctor may be having a bad day. Five doctors who each saw a slightly different set of patients, voting, are harder to fool.
DefinitionBagging. Fit each tree on a different random resample of the rows, then let the trees vote. Random forest. The same, and each split may only look at a random handful of the columns, so the trees resemble each other less.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
46

What Voting Actually Bought, With the Noise Shown

  • Every point is the mean of five runs that differ only in their random seed. The band runs from the worst run to the best.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
47

Read the Band Before You Read the Lines

  1. 1The widest band across seeds is 0.065. The largest gap between bagging and random forest at any size is 0.036.
  2. 2So on this data, changing the random seed moves the score nearly twice as much as choosing the method does.
  3. 3Textbooks show random forest above bagging. Here it is below, and the honest reading is that both are inside the same cloud of noise.
Watch outIf this figure had been one run per point, it would have shown a confident line and you would have believed it. One run is an anecdote. The band is the finding.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
48

Decide: What This Is Worth Reporting As

  1. 1Decision: report bagging and random forest as "about 0.80, give or take 0.03 depending on the seed", and do not claim one beat the other on this data.
  2. 2Report the seed, the number of trees and the number of rows with any ensemble number, or the result cannot be checked.
  3. 3When a difference you care about is smaller than your band, the answer is not a better model. It is more runs, or a bigger test set, or a different question.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems

52

The Gap Is the Story, Not the Score

  1. 1Every model loses about 20 points between training and test. Two different things cause that, and they need different answers.
  2. 2Overfitting: the model learned the training rows themselves. More data or a simpler model helps.
  3. 3Novelty: the test file contains attack types that were never in training. No amount of learning from the training file helps, and that is most of this gap.
NoteNSL-KDD was built this way on purpose. A test set that is a random slice of the training set would give you 0.99 and tell you nothing about next week's traffic.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
53

What Cross-Validation Adds, and What It Cannot

ModelFive folds on the training fileMeanSpread
decision tree, depth 50.9879, 0.9894, 0.9880, 0.9883, 0.98700.98810.0025
logistic regression0.9795, 0.9784, 0.9796, 0.9780, 0.97680.97850.0028
  1. 1The spread is the useful part: 0.9881 give or take 0.0025 is a claim, and 0.9881 alone is a hope.
  2. 2Both spreads are tiny, so neither model depends much on which rows it happened to train on.
  3. 3And both means are about 0.19 above the test score. Cross-validation measured stability, not the thing you actually care about.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
54

Decide: Which One Would You Deploy

  1. 1Need to explain a decision to a human at 3 in the morning? The depth-5 tree, 23 leaves.
  2. 2Need an answer in microseconds on every connection? Anything but k-NN, which is twenty times slower per row.
  3. 3Need the best chance on the rare families? Naive Bayes catches the most attacks here, at 0.669, and it is the cheapest to fit.
  4. 4Need the best test accuracy? The unlimited tree, by 0.003 over the depth-5 tree, which is not a reason.
Watch outYou now have five models that all beat the floor, and all miss about a third of the attacks. Accuracy cannot see that third. The next session is about the numbers that can.
CIS 3370 Intrusion Detection Systems
